intro: Mensuration in the papers is almost always **two flat figures joined by one length**: find that length in one figure and carry it to the other.
There are ten short lessons, in the order of what the papers set. The last three (other figures, solids, reshaping) were not asked in the sample papers; learn them after the rest.
What the papers ask (Stage A count in Quick revision: 23 IBPS Clerk papers and 12 sister papers, all memory-based):
| Two figures joined by one length (M1) | Confirmed, 14 papers | M1 (two lessons) |
| One rectangle from a ratio or relation (M2) | Confirmed, 7 papers | M2 |
| Sides change by a percent (M3) | Confirmed, 3 papers | M3 |
| Circles and semicircles (M4) | Confirmed, 3 papers | M4 |
| Squares in a ratio (M5) | Confirmed, 2 papers | M5 |
| Paths, borders and costs (M6) | Seen once | M6 |
| Other figures, solids, reshaping | Bank only | M7, M8, M9 |
after: That is the whole topic. The **Quick revision** tab has every formula on one page, the drills and the practice ladder.
Use pi = 22/7 unless the question says otherwise; it makes radii of 7, 14 and 21 come out cleanly.

lessons.title: One rectangle
lessons.plain: The starting point: find a rectangle's sides from a ratio, a difference, the perimeter or the area.
teach: Perimeter = 2 x (length + breadth). Area = length x breadth. Almost every question gives two facts and asks for a third.
**Half the perimeter is length + breadth.** Use it first. Perimeter 92 in the ratio 14 : 9: half is 46 = 23 parts, so a part is 2: 28 by 18.
**A difference instead of a ratio:** length 8 more than breadth, perimeter 40: l + b = 20 and l - b = 8, so b = 6 and l = 14.
**A ratio and the area:** parts x parts x unit². 8 : 5 with area 640: 40 unit² = 640, unit² = 16, unit = 4: 32 by 20.
Checked papers: seven papers (IBPS Clerk 2021, Dec 2021, Sep 2022; SBI Clerk Sep 2025; IBPS RRB Clerk Dec 2025 three times).

example.q: The breadth of a rectangle is 25% less than its length and its perimeter is 70 cm. Find its area.
steps: Half-perimeter 35 = 7 parts, so a part is 5: 20 by 15.
example.answer: 300 cm² (IBPS RRB Clerk Prelims 6 Dec 2025, memory-based).

check.q: A rectangle is 6 cm longer than it is broad, and its perimeter is 44 cm. What is its area?
check.why: l + b = 22, l - b = 6: 14 by 8, area 112. (120 takes the sides as 12 and 10.)

tags: The perimeter as a multiple of the breadth.

lessons.title: Two figures joined by one length
lessons.plain: New: the papers' favourite. One figure hands a length to another.
teach: Read for the joining sentence: "the side of the square is equal to the breadth of the rectangle", "2 cm more than the breadth", "the sum of the length and the side is 72".
Then three steps:
1. Solve the figure that is fully described.
2. Carry the shared length across, with any "more" or "less".
3. Finish the other figure: its perimeter, area or missing side.
Checked papers: fourteen papers. In the sample this is the commonest mensuration question by far.

example.q: The length of a rectangle is 10 cm more than its breadth, and its perimeter is 68 cm. The breadth is 2 cm less than the side of a square. Find the area of the square.
steps: l + b = 34 and l - b = 10, so the breadth is 12.

check.q: The perimeter of a square is 48 cm and its side equals the breadth of a rectangle of area 216 cm². What is the rectangle's length?
check.why: Side 12 = breadth, so length = 216 / 12 = 18. (16 uses the square's perimeter divided by 3.)

tags: The link runs through the perimeters.
A ratio and an area hand over a side.

lessons.title: Triangles and diagonals
lessons.plain: New: a right triangle or a diagonal hands over the length.
teach: Triangle area = base x height / 2, so **base = 2 x area / height**.
For right triangles, know these triples by sight; they save the square root: 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 7-24-25, 8-15-17, and their multiples (6-8-10, 10-24-26).
A square's diagonal is its side x √2. A rectangle's diagonal comes from the triple its sides make.
Checked papers: IBPS Clerk Oct 2025 and 2025 (Guidely) set the triangle-to-square form.

example.q: A right triangle has area 150 cm² and height 20 cm. Its base is the side of a square. Find the square's perimeter.

check.q: A rectangle is 15 cm long with a 17 cm diagonal. What is its area?
check.why: 8-15-17, so the breadth is 8: area 120. (255 multiplies the length by the diagonal.)

tags: Base from the area, then 3 less.
A square's diagonal, then a rectangle.

lessons.title: Circles and semicircles
lessons.plain: New: round figures. With pi = 22/7 the radius is usually a multiple of 7.
teach: | Figure | Perimeter | Area |
| circle | 44/7 x r | 22/7 x r x r |
| semicircle | 36/7 x r (the curve plus the diameter) | 11/7 x r x r |
So **semicircle perimeter 36 means r = 7**, 72 means r = 14, 108 means r = 21. **Circumference 88 means r = 14.**
"Circumference minus diameter" is 44/7 r - 2r = 30/7 r: 90 gives r = 21.
Checked papers: IBPS Clerk 2018, SBI Clerk Feb 2025 and IBPS RRB Clerk Dec 2025; semicircles also appear joined to rectangles (IBPS Clerk Sep 2022 and Oct 2025).

example.q: The circumferences of two circles are 88 m and 132 m. Find the sum of their radii.

check.q: A semicircle has perimeter 72 cm. What is its radius?
check.why: 36/7 x r = 72, so r = 14. (11.5 forgets the diameter and divides 72 by 2 x 22/7.)

tags: A semicircle hands its radius to a rectangle.

lessons.title: Squares in a ratio
lessons.plain: New: two squares compared. Lengths follow the ratio; areas follow its square.
teach: Sides in 5 : 9 mean perimeters and diagonals in 5 : 9 too, but **areas in 25 : 81**.
Turn the given difference into parts: diagonals differing by 16√2 is 4 parts x √2, so one part is 4.
The largest circle cut from a square has a diameter equal to the side.
Checked papers: IBPS Clerk Oct 2025, two shifts.

example.q: The sides of two squares are in the ratio 3 : 5 and their perimeters differ by 32 cm. Find the difference of their areas.
steps: Perimeters differ by 4 x 2 parts = 8 parts = 32, so a part is 4: sides 12 and 20.

check.q: The sides of two squares are in the ratio 2 : 3. What is the ratio of their areas?
check.why: Areas follow the square of the ratio: 4 : 9. (8 : 27 is the cube, used for volumes.)

tags: A circle cut from a square.

lessons.title: Sides change by a percent
lessons.plain: New: the sides grow or shrink, and the area or perimeter changes with them.
teach: **Multiply the factors.** Length up 20% (x 1.2), breadth down 10% (x 0.9): area x 1.08, an 8% rise. Never add the percents.
**Backwards:** length x 0.8 and area x 0.96 means breadth x 0.96 / 0.8 = 1.2, a 20% rise.
**Same factor on every side:** a square or cube side up 50% makes the area x 2.25 (up 125%) and the volume x 3.375.
**Perimeter after a change:** find the new sides first; perimeter does not follow the area's factor.
Checked papers: IBPS Clerk 2023 and Aug 2024, IBPS PO Aug 2025.

example.q: The length of a rectangle is increased by 25%. By what percent must the breadth be decreased to keep the area the same?

check.q: The side of a square is increased by 20%. By what percent does its area increase?
check.why: 1.2 x 1.2 = 1.44: a 44% rise. (40% adds the two 20s.)

tags: Find the sides, change them, then the perimeter.

lessons.title: Paths, borders and costs
lessons.plain: New: a strip around or across a figure, and the cost of covering or fencing it.
teach: **Path outside:** add twice the width to each side for the outer rectangle; path = outer - inner.
**Path inside:** subtract twice the width instead.
**Two roads crossing:** add both roads, then take off the square where they cross (it was counted twice).
**Cost** = area (or length, for fencing) x rate. When the cost is given, divide first to get the area.
**Tiles:** floor area / tile area, in the same units. **Wheels:** distance / circumference.
**Four walls of a room:** 2(l + b) x h.
Checked papers: IBPS Clerk 2019 set a path with a cost.

example.q: A garden 30 m by 20 m has a path 2 m wide all around it outside. Find the cost of paving the path at Rs 10 per m².

check.q: How many square tiles of side 50 cm are needed for a floor 10 m by 6 m?
check.why: Floor 1,000 cm by 600 cm: 20 x 12 = 240 tiles. (60 divides square metres by 1.)

tags: A path, backwards from the cost.

lessons.title: Rhombus, trapezium, equilateral triangle
lessons.plain: New: three more flat figures, each with one formula.
teach: | Figure | Area | Side or perimeter |
| rhombus, diagonals p and q | p x q / 2 | half-diagonals make a right triangle with the side |
| trapezium, parallel sides a and b, height h | (a + b) / 2 x h | add the four sides |
| equilateral triangle, side a | √3/4 x a x a | 3a |
No paper in the sample set these; they are common in practice sets.

example.q: The diagonals of a rhombus are 16 cm and 30 cm. Find its area and its side.

check.q: An equilateral triangle has perimeter 24 cm. What is its area?

lessons.title: Solids: volume and surface
lessons.plain: New: three-dimensional shapes. None was asked in the sample papers; learn them after the rest.
teach: | Solid | Volume | Surface |
| cuboid l, b, h | l x b x h | 2(lb + bh + lh) |
| cube a | a x a x a | 6 x a x a |
| cylinder r, h | 22/7 x r x r x h | curved 2 x 22/7 x r x h |
| cone r, h, slant l | 1/3 x 22/7 x r x r x h | curved 22/7 x r x l, with l from the triple of r and h |
| sphere r | 4/3 x 22/7 x r x r x r | 4 x 22/7 x r x r |
| hemisphere r | 2/3 x 22/7 x r x r x r | curved 2 x 22/7 x r x r |
Cube roots worth knowing: 343 = 7³, 512 = 8³, 729 = 9³, 1,331 = 11³, 1,728 = 12³.
Bank only: the banks hold 109 such questions, but no paper in the sample set one.

example.q: A cylinder has radius 7 cm and height 15 cm. Find its volume and curved surface.
steps: Curved surface = 2 x 22/7 x 7 x 15 = 660 cm².

check.q: A cube has volume 512 cm³. What is its total surface area?

lessons.title: Bent, melted, rolled
lessons.plain: New: one shape becomes another. Something stays the same; find it.
teach: | What happens | What stays the same |
| a wire is bent into a new shape | its length (the perimeter) |
| metal is melted and recast | the volume |
| a sheet is rolled into a cylinder | the rolled edge becomes the circumference; the other edge the height |
Write that quantity once for the old shape and once for the new, and set them equal.
For the same length of wire, a circle encloses more area than a square. That is a quick check on the options.
Bank only in this sample.

example.q: A wire bent into a square encloses 121 cm². It is rebent into a circle. Find the circle's area.
steps: Side 11, so the wire is 44 cm.

check.q: Eight small cubes of side 2 cm are melted into one cube. What is its side?
check.why: Volume 8 x 8 = 64, so the side is 4. (16 adds the sides.)

tags: Cone and cylinder of equal volume.
